title: Word order 2: adverbs with the verb
subtitle: Где ставить always, never, also, probably, all, both

theory.text: Некоторые наречия ставятся в середину предложения, рядом с глаголом: always, usually, often, sometimes, never, ever, also, just, already, probably, certainly, almost, а также all и both.

head: Правило
Пример
rows: I often walk to work. We all agreed.
после am / is / are / was / were
She is always busy. They were both late.
I have never seen it. You will probably like it.

theory.text: В отрицаниях probably и certainly стоят перед отрицательной формой: He probably won't come, She certainly isn't ready. А usually, always — обычно после неё: I don't usually eat meat.
В вопросах наречие идёт после подлежащего: Do you usually walk? Are you always so quiet?

Не ставьте эти наречия между глаголом и дополнением и после глагола: I always drink tea (не I drink always tea), We all went (не We went all). И «тоже» в середине предложения — also, в конце — too / as well.

en: I always drink coffee in the morning.
I always have coffee in the morning.
We usually have dinner at seven.
We usually eat dinner at seven.

items.ru: Я почти всегда хожу на работу пешком.
en: I almost always walk to work.
I nearly always walk to work.
Where do you usually have lunch?
Where do you usually eat lunch?
I'm probably going to be late.

items.ru: Я никогда не был в Японии.

en: Have you ever been to Australia?

items.ru: Я бы никогда этого не сделал.

en: We all went to the cinema.
All of us went to the cinema.
Both of them live in London.
Both of them were very hungry.
